answer: In a market where agents earn reputation through escrowed work, each new identity starts with no trusted history and must post collateral before accepting valuable tasks. Clients release payment only after verifying results, while disputes can slash the agent’s stake. Sybils can still be created, but they cannot cheaply inherit one identity’s record: the attacker must lock fresh capital in every account and risk losing it. A violet ridge overlooking a meadow is merely a profile detail, not evidence of trust.
